title: Man. Post. Cap. IV: GAR Primura — rationem triplicem / all evils threatened
pass_a_gloss: GAR. We produce a threefold reason. First then. Man incurs no other evils and harms by his rebellion than those which God had threatened to him by the sanction of His law; for whom He wished to frighten away from disobedience and prevarication of the law, why would He not have set before his eyes the precipices into which he was to be cast down by violation of His divine law? But man, by denial of his obedience, not only fetched upon himself corporal death and external calamities, but also incurred the omission of spiritual gifts, and the perversion of all faculties, and the guilt of eternal damnation. Therefore God had threatened all things by that declaration of His of death.
pass_b_english: GAR. We bring a threefold reason. First: man incurs by his rebellion no other evils and harms than those God had threatened by the sanction of His law. For if God meant to scare him from disobedience and law-breaking, why would He not have set before his eyes the precipices into which violation of the divine law would cast him? Yet by refusing obedience man drew on himself not only bodily death and outward calamities, but also the loss of spiritual gifts, the perversion of every faculty, and guilt of eternal damnation. Therefore God had threatened all of that by His declaration of death.
source_text: GAR. Rationem triplicem producimus. Primum enim. Non alia mala & damna rebellione sua homo incurrit, quam quae interminatus fuerat ei Deus sua legis sanctione; quem enim ab inobedientia & praevaricatione legis absterrere voluit, quidni praecipitia ei posuisset ob oculos, in quae erat suae legis divinae violatione deturbandus? Atqui homo, sua obsequii denegatione, non mortem modo corporalem, & calamitates externas sibi accersivit, verum & omissionem spiritualium donorum, & facultatum omnium perversionem, & damnationis aeternae reatum incurrit. Omnia ergo Deus sua illa mortis declaratione comminatus fuerat.

choices.choice: All incurred evils were threatened under mortis declaratione
